rfi.title: EU unveils plan to cut dependence on US and Asian technology
rfi.description: Europe is launching a sweeping push to reduce its dependence on American and Asian technology, with plans to boost homegrown chips, cloud computing and artificial intelligence while keeping greater control over data and key digital services.

rfi.title: El Nino threat grows as Europe prepares for another hot summer
rfi.description: The warming El Nino climate phenomenon is likely to develop by the end of August, the United Nations' weather agency said, raising the risk of extreme weather as Europe faces another summer on the front line of climate change.

rfi.title: EU tightens migration rules, eyes strategic enlargement in Balkans
rfi.description: The European Union has reached a deal on tougher migration rules that would allow countries to set up so-called “return hubs” outside the bloc, a move hailed by supporters as a practical answer to stalled deportations, but denounced by rights groups as a dangerous step towards offshore detention. Meanwhile, the question of EU enlargement is also on the cards at a Western Balkans summit.

rfi.title: France bans Israeli offensive weapons on Europe's largest arms trade show
rfi.description: France has banned the display of Israeli offensive weapons at the 2026 edition of the Eurosatory international defence and security exhibition which opens on 15 June.

rfi.title: WHO seeks more aid for Congo as ebola outbreak continues to spread
rfi.description: The head of the World Health Organization  met with Félix Tshisekedi on Monday to discuss the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ebola outbreak, as an aid agency warned the epidemic was likely far larger than official figures suggest. The government said confirmed Ebola cases had risen to 321.

rfi.title: French health minister promises fast track access to mental health for youth
rfi.description: France's Health Minister Stéphanie Rist announced on Tuesday that the government would fast-track access to mental health appointments for young people. She promised that those identified by staff in the national education system as having mental health problems would be seen by a professional within 24 to 48 hours.

rfi.title: Mozambique claims five of its nationals killed killed in South Africa 'xenophobic attacks'
rfi.description: Mozambique has claimed that five of its nationals were killed in xenophobic attacks in South Africa at the weekend, as efforts got under way on Tuesday to repatriate hundreds of others.

rfi.title: New York Times chief slams AI companies for 'theft' of intellectual property
rfi.description: The head of The New York Times newspaper launched a scathing attack on artificial intelligence companies, accusing them of "shameless theft of intellectual property" and of threatening journalism. He was speaking at a global media congress on Monday in the southern French city of Marseille.

rfi.title: Cattelan’s famous taped banana stolen from French museum
rfi.description: A museum in eastern France has filed a police complaint after a banana forming the centrepiece of Maurizio Cattelan’s multimillion-dollar conceptual artwork "Comedian" was stolen from an exhibition.

rfi.title: Africa's finest: Morocco, African champions by ruling
rfi.description: Morocco arrive at the first 48-team World Cup as Africa's highest-ranked side in the Fifa standings. In the second of a nine-part series on African squads at the tournament, RFI profiles a nation making its seventh World Cup appearance.

rfi.title: Gulf states arrested over 1,000 for Iran war social media posts: Amnesty
rfi.description: More than 1,000 people have been arrested across Gulf states for sharing information or opinions related to the Iran-US-Israeli war, in what Amnesty International has described as a “widespread crackdown” on freedom of expression.

rfi.title: Court rejects Rwanda €115mn claim against Britain over migrant deal
rfi.description: An international court on Monday rejected a claim by Rwanda for Britain to pay more than £100 million (€115million) it said London still owed from a scrapped deal to deport migrants.

rfi.title: Guineans denounce an 'electoral farce' after low turnout in legislative polls
rfi.description: Legislative and municipal elections were held in Guinea on Sunday to complete the process of returning constitutional order to the country after the December 2025 presidential election While this double ballot took place without major incident, voter turnout was low.

rfi.title: Ethiopia goes to the polls with the result widely seen as a foregone conclusion
rfi.description: Ethiopia holds parliamentary and regional elections on Monday that analysts expect Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's party to win by a large margin, despite significant unrest across much of the country.

rfi.title: PSG celebrations marred by violence as French authorities report 890 arrests
rfi.description: French authorities have arrested over 890 people after outbreaks of violence followed Paris Saint-Germain’s Champions League victory on Saturday, as the government defended its policing operation amid sharp criticism from the right.

rfi.title: France boards fourth Russian oil tanker as crackdown on ‘shadow fleet’ continues
rfi.description: The French Navy has boarded another oil tanker from Russia as Paris steps up its campaign against Moscow’s so-called "shadow fleet" of vessels suspected of evading international sanctions.

rfi.title: France weighs tougher safeguards against child abuse in schools
rfi.description: French lawmakers will on Monday debate tougher protections against sexual abuse in schools and after-school programmes, as a series of scandals increases pressure on the government to strengthen safeguards.

rfi.title: First contact: Curaçao’s rise to the global stage
rfi.description: Curaçao will make its World Cup debut at the 2026 tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada. In the first instalment of a four-part series, RFI looks at the journey of the smallest nation to qualify for the competition in its 96-year history.

The east African nation had sued the current UK government for more than £100m, claiming it was owed after a breach of an agreement.

Teachers associated with CNTE union were marching toward Zócalo for salary raises and reversal of pension laws

Riot police fired teargas at teachers who were marching toward Mexico City’s historic Zócalo plaza, just days before the square is expected to host the 2026 World Cup “Fan Fest”. The incident is the second time police have clashed with teachers in the past week, and more conflict is likely as Mexico City prepares to hold the opening game of the Fifa World Cup on 11 June.

guardian.description:
Success of far-right presidential candidate, Abelardo de la Espriella, suggests some voters are ‘fed up with politics’

The far-right lawyer Abelardo de la Espriella and the leftwing senator Iván Cepeda have just under three weeks to compete for the roughly 3.6m votes that did not go to either of them in the first round of Colombia’s presidential election.

That is no insignificant number, given that De la Espriella’s lead over Cepeda amounted to little more than 670,000 votes – 43.

Powerful winds and rain expected in parts of Japan and Australia, while temperatures in Spain could hit 40C

euronews.description: Economics analyst Osama Rizvi believes the chance of markets getting "worse" or "ugly" is "more than getting better" due to the changing situation between the US and Iran. According to Rizvi, economic confidence is "going down" in Europe.

euronews.title: EBRD lowers growth forecast as Iran war energy shock continues to hit economies
euronews.description: Economic growth across the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development's regions is expected to slow more sharply than previously forecast this year, largely due to higher inflation linked to the Iran war, which has pushed up energy prices. Inflation across the bank's regions rose to 6.4%.

euronews.title: ‘If you throw trash, you lose cash’: Tokyo tourist district introduces littering fines
euronews.description: Visitors caught dropping rubbish in Tokyo’s popular Shibuya ward will now be fined on the spot as authorities battle the side effects of Japan’s record tourism boom.

euronews.title: French artist JR's giant 'cave' installation in Paris appears damaged
euronews.description: Strong winds and heavy rain damaged artist JR’s giant “La Caverne” installation covering Paris’ Pont Neuf bridge, forcing organisers to postpone its public opening scheduled for June 6.

euronews.title: You can’t miss these: Best World Cup 2026 squad announcement videos
euronews.description: From the Beatles to the African savannah, some national federations were inspired and chose even Royals to annouce the final squad lists for the World Cup.

euronews.title: Which European countries attract the most foreign investment?
euronews.description: Foreign investment is widely seen as a key driver of economic growth, innovation and job creation. But which countries are winning the race for international investors, and how is Europe's position changing in an increasingly competitive global market?

euronews.title: New US tariff plan targets EU and dozens of economies over forced labour imports
euronews.description: The EU and UK are among the economies targeted by a new US tariff proposal linked to forced labour imports, potentially reopening trade tensions just weeks after Brussels reached a deal with Washington.

euronews.title: Europe Today: Magyar softens on Ukraine as EU prepares new Russia sanctions
euronews.description: Hungary could lift its veto on the opening of Ukraine's EU accession talks if Kyiv accepts to protect minority rights for the Hungarian community in Ukraine. Meanwhile, the EU is preparing more sanctions against Russia. Angela Skujins speaks to the EU's Sanctions Envoy, David O'Sullivan.

euronews.title: UK: Police and protesters clash at Southampton rally over student killing
euronews.description: Clashes broke out between protesters and police in Southampton after the release of bodycam footage linked to the fatal stabbing of student Henry Nowak sparked public anger.

euronews.title: EU vs China: Can Europe break its supply chain dependence?
euronews.description: Brussels wants new rules that would make European companies spread out their supply chains rather than rely on a single main supplier. The EU says its trade relationship with China is now "unsustainable." Watch the video.

euronews.title: Spain probe targets Socialist party payments to consultant Leire Díez, 3 times more than admitted
euronews.description: The PSOE paid Díez nearly 45,000 euros for communications work between 2015 and 2017, according to documents sent to a Madrid court, as judges probe an alleged scheme to sway cases affecting the party and the government.

euronews.title: Venice Biennale 61: Patti Smith and Soundwalk Collective's ritual performance
euronews.description: Patti Smith performed texts and hymns by Saint Hildegard of Bingen, a 12th-century Benedictine nun, at the official opening of the Holy See's Vatican Pavilion.

euronews.title: Waiting times for healthcare in Europe: The worst countries ranked
euronews.description: Waiting times for treatment in some European countries can run for years. This has real consequences for patients, experts warn. Euronews Health takes a close look at waiting times across several categories.

euronews.title: A flamboyance of flamingos flocks to Venice Lagoon thanks to EU wetlands restoration project
euronews.description: 24,000 pink flamingos were spotted in the famous lagoon in 2025 - 6,000 more than in 2024.

lemonde.title: Guerre en Ukraine : la Russie profite du déficit de Patriot pour frapper Kiev et Dnipro avec des missiles hypersoniques
lemonde.description: Lors de son attaque massive du 2 juin, qui a tué 23 personnes, l’armée russe a utilisé des projectiles qui ne peuvent être interceptés que par le système antibalistique américain. Volodymyr Zelensky a demandé, une nouvelle fois, à ses alliés occidentaux de lui fournir davantage d’intercepteurs de ce type.

lemonde.title: L’administration Trump, sous la pression des élus républicains, recule sur la création d’un fonds d’indemnisation dont auraient pu bénéficier les émeutiers du Capitole
lemonde.description: A moins de six mois des élections de mi-mandat, de nombreux sénateurs du Parti républicain s’étaient opposés à la mise en place de ce fonds, doté de 1,8 milliard de dollars. Le projet était par ailleurs gelé par une juge fédérale.

lemonde.title: L’OFCE propose un autre outil que la taxe Zucman pour mieux imposer les plus riches
lemonde.description: Pour que les ménages très aisés n’échappent pas à l’impôt, les économistes Guillaume Allègre et Xavier Timbeau, de l’Observatoire français des conjonctures économiques, suggèrent de taxer non pas le patrimoine, mais l’ensemble des revenus. Y compris les plus-values réalisées lors des donations et successions.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : l’aéroport du Koweït attaqué par des drones iraniens, les Etats-Unis disent avoir intercepté des missiles dans la région du Golfe
lemonde.description: Plusieurs personnes ont été blessées et « des dommages matériels graves » provoqués par des drones à l’aéroport international, selon les autorités koweïtiennes. L’armée américaine dit avoir neutralisé des tirs de missiles et de drones visant notamment Bahreïn, et mené des frappes en représailles.

lemonde.title: Défense : le gouvernement enregistre un revers inattendu au Sénat sur la loi de programmation militaire
lemonde.description: La droite, dont la demande de rallonge globale de 50 milliards d’euros pour les armées n’a pas été votée, a réagi en faisant rejeter l’article phare du projet. Celui-ci actait la trajectoire budgétaire jusqu’en 2030, en incluant une enveloppe de 36 milliards d’euros supplémentaires.

lemonde.title: Les films à l’affiche : « Bouchra », « Bait », « La Bataille de Gaulle. L’âge de fer », « En nous »…
lemonde.description: Chaque mercredi, dans La Matinale, les journalistes cinéma du « Monde » livrent leurs critiques des films à découvrir en salle. Aujourd’hui, notamment, le réalisateur britannique Mark Jenkin capte une lutte des classes sourde.

lemonde.title: Au Royaume-Uni, l’extrême droite instrumentalise les errances de la police après le meurtre d’un étudiant par un jeune Sikh
lemonde.description: Nigel Farage, le chef de file du parti Reform UK, a dénoncé un racisme « anti-Blancs » après la diffusion d’une vidéo montrant des policiers menotter un jeune homme agonisant qui venait d’être poignardé par un jeune Sikh. Ce dernier avait faussement prétendu avoir subi une attaque raciste.

lemonde.title: La santé des présidents, un secret d’Etat
lemonde.description: Dans « Le Crépuscule des dieux », Patrice Duhamel révèle les derniers mystères qui entourent les maladies des présidents, notamment l’un d’entre eux, Georges Pompidou, grâce au journal du professeur Jean Bernard.

lemonde.title: Chlordécone : le Parlement reconnaît la « part de responsabilité » de l’Etat dans le scandale aux Antilles
lemonde.description: Le texte, adopté à l’unanimité, contraint l’Etat à œuvrer à la dépollution des terres. Il pose aussi comme « objectif » l’indemnisation des victimes, sans en faire une obligation. Plus de 90 % de la population adulte des Antilles est contaminée par ce pesticide.

lemonde.title: Régulation de l’IA : Donald Trump trouve un compromis pour satisfaire à la fois sa base MAGA et les entreprises de la tech
lemonde.description: Un décret donne trente jours à l’Etat fédéral pour évaluer les nouveaux modèles d’intelligence artificielle avant leur mise sur le marché. Le président américain cède ainsi à ses partisans, qui lui demandaient de réguler le secteur, mais sur un temps bien plus court que les quatre-vingt-dix jours prévus par un précédent texte.

lemonde.title: Avec le soutien de Nathalie Kosciusko-Morizet, Edouard Philippe veut apparaître en rassembleur de la droite et du centre
lemonde.description: Absente depuis neuf ans de la scène politique, « NKM » effectue son retour derrière le candidat Horizons à la présidentielle en 2027. L’occasion pour celui-ci de montrer qu’il peut susciter des ralliements, à la différence de Gabriel Attal et de Bruno Retailleau.

lemonde.title: Au Danemark, un troisième mandat pour la première ministre, Mette Frederiksen
lemonde.description: Après des tractations historiquement longues, la patronne des sociaux-démocrates danois a réussi à former une coalition de centre gauche, incluant quatre partis, dans le cadre d’un paysage politique éclaté.

lemonde.title: Polémique autour de Xenia Fedorova, chroniqueuse pro-Kremlin : des eurodéputés réclament des sanctions européennes
lemonde.description: La chroniqueuse des médias Bolloré, ancienne patronne de la branche française de la chaîne russe RT France, est accusée de recourir à la « désinformation coordonnée et à la manipulation de l’information ».

lemonde.title: En Tunisie, Rached Ghannouchi, figure de l’opposition et déjà incarcéré, a été condamné à la perpétuité
lemonde.description: M. Ghannouchi, 84 ans, et d’autres cadres du parti islamiste Ennahdha ont été condamnés, mardi, à des peines de prison allant de dix ans à la perpétuité pour terrorisme, ont annoncé la formation et des médias.

lemonde.title: L’ancien footballeur David Beckham va avoir son étoile à Hollywood
lemonde.description: La cérémonie, à laquelle participeront son épouse, Victoria, et l’acteur Tom Cruise, est prévue le 12 juin, jour de l’entrée en lice à Los Angeles de la sélection américaine dans la Coupe du monde. Elle célébrera l’« influence durable dans le sport, le divertissement et la culture mondiale » de l’Anglais, âgé de 51 ans.

lemonde.title: Droits de douane : l’administration Trump propose de nouvelles taxes en invoquant la lutte contre le travail forcé
lemonde.description: Washington souhaite imposer de nouveaux droits de douane à soixante économies, dont la Chine et l’Union européenne, ayant échoué à instaurer une interdiction des importations de biens issus du travail forcé.

france24fr.title: En direct : des drones ukrainiens visent Saint-Pétersbourg, une frappe meurtrière près de Donetsk
france24fr.description: Des drones ukrainiens ont ciblé mercredi des sites énergétiques et militaires à Saint-Pétersbourg, où s'ouvre le traditionnel forum économique rassemblant de nombreux dirigeants russes, ont indiqué des responsables russes et ukrainiens. Plus tôt, une frappe de drone ukrainienne sur un car reliant Moscou à Simferopol, en Crimée annexée par la Russie, a fait sept morts. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: En Algérie, le harcèlement judiciaire des opposants
france24fr.description: A la Une de la presse, ce mercredi 3 juin, l’alerte de l’ONU, qui redoute un retour d’El Nino dans les mois à venir. L’inquiétude grandissante face aux atermoiements de Donald Trump vis-à-vis de l’Iran, et à l’amateurisme de sa diplomatie.  La colère de l’opposition algérienne face à un régime qui cadenasse chaque jour un peu plus le pays. Les députés français face à un scandale sanitaire passé, et un autre peut-être en cours. Et la «fashion battle» entre footballeurs français et anglais.

france24fr.title: Roland-Garros : Alexander Zverev rêve toujours d'un premier Grand Chelem
france24fr.description: Alexander Zverev a battu Rafael Jodar (7-6, 6-1, 6-3) en quarts de finale à Roland-Garros. Qualifié pour la demi-finale, il peut rêver d'un premier titre du Grand Chelem.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle en Colombie : Trump soutient le candidat d'extrême droite Abelardo de la Espriella
france24fr.description: Le président américain Donald Trump a apporté mardi son soutien à Abelardo de la Espriella, candidat d'extrême droite à la présidentielle colombienne, qui affrontera le favori de gauche Ivan Cepeda au second tour le 21 juin.

france24fr.title: En direct : l'armée américaine dit avoir repoussé des attaques de missiles iraniens dans le Golfe
Moyen-Orient en direct : l'aéroport du Koweït touché par des drones iraniens, le trafic suspendu
france24fr.description: Des drones iraniens ont touché l'aéroport international du Koweït, faisant plusieurs blessés et entraînant une suspension du trafic aérien, a annoncé mercredi l'armée koweïtienne. La veille, l'armée américaine avait affirmé avoir repoussé plusieurs attaques iraniennes, par missiles et drones, contre ses bases et ses alliés dans la région, et avoir répliqué en bombardant au sol une île iranienne. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Trump - Netanyahou : je t'aime, moi non plus !
france24fr.description: Selon le média Axios, Donald Trump aurait eu une conversation houleuse avec Benyamin Netanyahou au sujet de la guerre menée par Israël au Liban. Il aurait notamment lâché ces mots : "Putain qu’est-ce que tu fous ? Tu es complètement fou !" Si les deux hommes se connaissent de longue date, leur relation n'a jamais été aussi tendue.

france24fr.title: À Paris, deux morts dans la Seine en marge des célébrations du sacre du PSG
france24fr.description: Selon un nouveau bilan publié mardi, deux personnes ont été retrouvées mortes après être tombées dans la Seine ce week-end en marge des célébrations du sacre du PSG en Ligue des champions.

france24fr.title: L'administration Trump renonce finalement à son "fonds anti-instrumentalisation" de la justice
france24fr.description: Le ministre américain de la Justice par intérim a annoncé mardi que le gouvernement Trump renonçait finalement à son très polémique "fonds anti-instrumentalisation" de la justice. Une juge avait déjà bloqué ce projet, considéré par l'opposition démocrate comme une "caisse noire" visant à dédommager les assaillants du Capitole.

france24fr.title: IA : Anthropic rend son moteur ultra-performant Mythos accessible à l’UE
france24fr.description: On connaissait déjà Claude, mais la start-up américaine Anthropic a développé un nouveau modèle d’IA, Mythos, encore en phase de test. Pensé pour être spécialiste du code, il s’est révélé encore plus performant que ses créateurs ne l’imaginaient, et capable de détecter des failles informatiques jusque-là indétectées, à une vitesse et une échelle exceptionnelles. Ces performances en font un outil extraordinaire mais qui peut se transformer en arme s’il tombe entre de mauvaises mains, alors Anthro

france24fr.title: Coupe du Monde : gazon maudit ?
france24fr.description: Dans 9 jours débutera la Coupe du Monde de football.  Sur les réseaux sociaux, des internautes, vidéos à l'appui, s'interrogent sur la qualité de la pelouse des stades qui accueilleront les rencontres. Mais les images présentées ne prouvent rien. Explications.

france24fr.title: Remaniement ministériel au Sénégal : une nouvelle équipe de 30 ministres dont 4 femmes
france24fr.description: Fin du suspense au Sénégal. Après 11 jours d'attente, Président Bassirou Diomaye Faye a composé ce lundi, un nouveau gouvernement. Une équipe sans la participation du Pastef, le parti dirigé par son ancien Premier ministre, nouveau président de l'Assemblée nationale et compagnon de route de longue date, Ousmane Sonko. Un gouvernement de 30 ministres dont 4 femmes.

france24fr.title: Pollution au chlordécone aux Antilles : le Parlement reconnaît une responsabilité de l'État
france24fr.description: Le Parlement a adopté, mardi, une proposition de loi visant à reconnaître la "part de responsabilité" de l'État dans le scandale du chlordécone aux Antilles, malgré une ambition amoindrie en cours d'examen au Sénat.

france24fr.title: Une proposition de loi pour limiter l'exposition des Français au cadmium
france24fr.description: Les Français sont surexposés au cadmium, responsable notamment de l'augmentation des cancers du pancréas. Ce métal lourd est répandu dans les champs par le biais des engrais phosphatés. La concentration maximale autorisée en France est de 90mg de cadmium par kilo d'engrais. L'ANSES préconise un plafond à 20mg seulement. Une proposition de loi a été adoptée en commission à l'Assemblée Nationale. Elle vise à réduire drastiquement les concentrations autorisées.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : même sans Sonko, le président Diomaye Faye a des chances de gouverner sans blocages
france24fr.description: Le président sénégalais, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, a fait, lundi, un pas supplémentaire vers la rupture avec son ex-Premier ministre Ousmane Sonko en formant, sans son assentiment pour une particpation du Pastef, un nouveau gouvernement. Selon les analystes, l'exécutif pourrait toutefois fonctionner sans subir de blocage décisif de son ex-allié.

france24fr.title: Cancer du pancréas : le daraxonrasib, un espoir pour retarder la progression de la maladie
france24fr.description: Présenté au congrès international d'oncologie de Chicago, un nouveau traitement contre le cancer du pancréas, le daraxonrasib, a été accueilli comme "un progrès majeur". Pour cause, cet anticancéreux pourrait doubler l'espérance de vie de certains patients et ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives pour le traitement d'autres cancers. Explications.

france24fr.title: Donald Trump assistera au dîner des correspondants de la Maison Blanche reprogrammé en juillet
france24fr.description: Le président américain Donald Trump sera bien présent au dîner des correspondants de la Maison Blanche, reprogrammé au 24 juillet après la fusillade qui avait éclaté fin avril. Cette fois, le gala sera "plus intime" et le dispositif sera "nettement renforcé".

france24fr.title: Guerre hybride : l'atout de Vladimir Poutine ?
france24fr.description: En Ukraine, la guerre se poursuit. La Russie multiplie ses offensives et a mené, la nuit dernière, une attaque de drones contre le territoire ukrainien. Parallèlement, le pétrolier russe Tagor, en provenance de Mourmansk et arraisonné par la Marine nationale ce week-end, est arrivé ce matin en baie de Douarnenez. Dans le même temps, à l'est de l'Europe, un drone russe chargé d'explosifs a pénétré l'espace aérien roumain avant de s'écraser sur un immeuble, faisant deux blessés.

zeit.title: Krieg gegen die Ukraine: Ukraine trifft Ziele in St. Petersburg vor Wirtschaftsgipfel
zeit.description: Vor dem Wirtschaftsforum in St. Petersburg hat die Ukraine Ziele in der Stadt mit Drohnen angegriffen. Laut lokalen Behörden gibt es Verletzte. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Ötzi-Mumie: Forschende finden Hinweise auf lebende Mikroorganismen an Ötzi-Mumie
zeit.description: Wissenschaftlern haben die Gesamtheit der Mikroorganismen untersucht, die die Ötzi Mumie besiedelten. Dabei fanden sie neben altem Erbgut auch jüngere DNA Spuren.

zeit.title: Appell an Filmemacher: Schwarzer an Wenders: Schneide endlich die zwei Minuten raus
Beim Einkaufen verloren: 19-Jährige gibt verlorene Handtasche mit 5.750 Euro zurück
Fußball-Bundesliga: Zingler über Meistertitel der Männer: «Nicht mehr möglich»
Christopher Street Day: «Starkes Signal»: CSD bleibt mehr als nur ein Straßenfest
Ukrainekarte aktuell: Warmes Wetter beeinflusst Kämpfe in Südukraine
zeit.description: Der Sommerbeginn hat Folgen für den Einsatz von Drohnen im Kriegsgebiet. Trotz andauernder Kämpfe nahmen weder die Ukraine noch Russland neue Gebiete ein.

zeit.title: Kriminalität: Mutmaßliches Sexualdelikt an Schule – Haftbefehl aufgehoben
Armutsbericht: Senatorin Kiziltepe: Hohe Armutsquote «Weckruf» für Politik
Erster Transfer: Basketball: MBC verpflichtet Spielmacher Radojicic
Lebensgefährlich verletzt: Nach Stromschlag: Teenager weiter in kritischem Zustand
Fahrradhelm: Mehr als die Hälfte laut Umfrage für Helmpflicht auf dem Fahrrad
zeit.description: In einer Umfrage gibt nur gut ein Drittel der Fahrradfahrer an, immer einen Helm zu tragen. Trotzdem sprechen sich 54 Prozent für eine Fahrradhelmpflicht aus.

zeit.title: Umweltpolitik in Deutschland: »Hätte es in meiner Macht gelegen, mehr Vorsorge zu treffen?«
zeit.description: Angela Merkel hält eine Festrede zum 40-jährigen Jubiläum des Umweltministeriums. Sie hat eine Botschaft an die Klimaaktivisten – und auch an die eigene Partei.

zeit.title: Einbürgerungen in Deutschland: 2025 so viele Menschen wie nie eingebürgert
zeit.description: Im vergangenen Jahr sind 332.500 Menschen in Deutschland eingebürgert worden – ein neuer Höchststand. Die meisten von ihnen hatten zuvor die syrische Staatsbürgerschaft.

zeit.title: IWU-Studie zur Mieterbelastung: Mieterbund beklagt Überlastung von Millionen Menschen durch Wohnkosten
zeit.description: Fast jeder dritte Mieter gibt laut Mieterbund mehr als 30 Prozent seines Nettoeinkommens für Wohnkosten aus. Die hohen Kosten für Miete träfen Geringverdiener besonders.

nzz.title: Gouverneurswahl in Kalifornien: Der Republikaner Steve Hilton qualifiziert sich wohl für die Stichwahl im November
nzz.description: Kalifornien wählt die Nachfolge des demokratischen Gouverneurs Gavin Newsom. Laut vorläufigen Resultaten qualifiziert sich neben Hilton auch der ehemalige demokratische Gesundheitsminister Xavier Becerra für die entscheidende Runde.

nzz.title: «Ich habe sie gepackt, mit dem Halsband über die Türklinke gehängt und dann zugeschlagen» Junge Hundehalterin belastet sich mit Sprachnachrichten selber
nzz.description: Vor Gericht sagt die Frau, es habe sich nur um verbalen Stressabbau gehandelt. Mit der Realität habe das nichts zu tun.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - Gas weiterhin doppelt so teuer wie vor der Krise – die aktuellen Zahlen zur Energieversorgung in Deutschland
nzz.description: Wie wirken sich Energiewende und globale Krisen auf Strom- und Gaspreise aus? Hier gibt es jeden Tag die aktuellen Zahlen.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Verletzte am Flughafen von Kuwait nach iranischem Drohnenangriff +++ US-Militär wehrt iranische Luftangriffe ab
nzz.description: Die USA und Israel haben Iran angegriffen. Teheran hat heftige Gegenangriffe lanciert. Gegenwärtig gilt eine Waffenruhe. Die Folgen des Konflikts sind weltweit spürbar. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.title: Rassismus gegen Weisse? In Grossbritannien erschüttert das massive Fehlverhalten eines Polizisten die Menschen
nzz.description: Nachdem ein Sikh einen Studenten niedergestochen hat, verhaftet der Uniformierte den Sterbenden Henry Nowak statt den Täter. Der Reform-UK-Chef Farage spricht von Weissen-Diskriminierung. Am Dienstagabend kam es zu Protesten.

nzz.title: Die USA künden 10 Prozent Zölle für die EU und 12,5 Prozent für die Schweiz an – Trump baut die Drohkulisse wieder auf
nzz.description: Nach den Zöllen ist vor den Zöllen. Nachdem das Oberste Gericht der USA frühere Zölle für illegal erklärt hat, erhebt Trump nun neue Zölle. Der offizielle Grund: Zwangsarbeit.

nzz.title: Trendwende bei der 10-Millionen-Schweiz. Plötzlich sind die Gegner im Vorteil
nzz.description: Die zweite Umfrage der SRG deutet auf eine Ablehnung hin – allerdings mit einem Vorbehalt.

nzz.title: Die Explosion von Jeff Bezos’ Rakete bringt die Mondpläne der Nasa durcheinander. Auch das amerikanische Militär ist besorgt
nzz.description: Eine Mondlandung bis 2028 hängt nun von einer einzigen Firma ab: SpaceX. Doch auch sie liegt hinter dem Zeitplan.

nzz.title: Die Kreuzritterburg Beaufort ist ein Wunderwerk des Festungsbaus – und ein strategischer Hotspot im Nahen Osten. Jetzt hat Israel sie erobert
nzz.description: Im 12. Jahrhundert eroberten christliche Ritter das Kastell Beaufort in Südlibanon. Im Lauf der Zeit wurde es von Kreuzfahrern, Osmanen und der PLO genutzt. Und jetzt von der israelischen Armee.

nzz.title: Es ist der erste Deal nach Buffett: Berkshire Hathaway kauft den US-Häuslebauer Taylor Morrison
nzz.description: Die grösste Beteiligungsgesellschaft der Welt setzt darauf, dass sich der schwächelnde amerikanische Immobilienmarkt bald erholt.

nzz.title: Wirtschaftsstandort Schweiz: Das Parlament will die Unternehmen entlasten
nzz.description: Die Schweiz soll steuerlich attraktiver werden und Regulierungskosten senken. Von diesen Vorstössen im Parlament könnten multinationale Unternehmen und KMU profitieren.

nzz.title: Sie sind gekommen, um zu gehen: Grenzgänger prägen Genf und Annemasse
nzz.description: Fast zwei Drittel der Bevölkerung von Annemasse arbeiten in der Schweiz. Nun fürchtet die französische Grenzstadt, dass die Zahl der Grenzgänger bei einer Annahme der 10-Millionen-Initiative der SVP noch weiter zunehmen könnte.

nzz.title: PODCAST «NZZ GEOPOLITIK» - Weltraum-Anarchie: Wer kontrolliert die Tausenden neuen Satelliten?
nzz.description: Die Kommerzialisierung im All eröffnet der Wissenschaft neue Möglichkeiten. Doch gleichzeitig verschärfen sie die geopolitischen Spannungen und erhöhen das Risiko von Kollisionen. Die aktuelle Folge des Podcasts «NZZ Geopolitik» erklärt den Rausch im All.

nzz.title: «Nein, ich bin nicht Satoshi» — aber ohne Adam Back gäbe es den Bitcoin wohl nicht
nzz.description: Der Krypto-Pionier und Wegbegleiter des Bitcoin-Erfinders Satoshi Nakamoto will mit seiner Firma an die Börse. Er glaubt an das digitale Gold und hält die Bedrohung durch Quantencomputer für übertrieben.

nzz.title: Kambodscha pflegt sein Image und gibt sich milde gegenüber seinem prominentesten Oppositionellen
nzz.description: Die Regierung entlässt auf Druck des Westens einen wichtigen Kritiker aus dem Gefängnis. Die strukturellen Probleme aber bleiben.

spiegel.title: Debattenkultur: Das Ende der kulturellen Hegemonie – ein Leitartikel von Tobias Rapp
spiegel.description: Die Vorstellung, man würde Rechte wie Peter Thiel stoppen, indem man ihnen ein Podium verwehrt, ist absurd. Dafür bräuchte es eine Hegemonie der Linken. Die gibt es aber längst nicht mehr.

spiegel.title: Ostervilm vor Rügen: Militärplattform im Meer zu verkaufen
spiegel.description: Von einer eigenen Insel haben wohl schon viele geträumt – und den Gedanken schnell abgetan. Nun steht immerhin ein künstliches Eiland in der Ostsee zum Verkauf. Mindestgebot: 39.000 Euro.

spiegel.title: Papst Leo XIV. ernennt Medienmanagerin zur Kommunikationschefin im Vatikan
spiegel.description: Die Journalistin Maria Montserrat Alvarado soll in Zukunft die Kommunikation des Vatikans steuern. Sie ist die erste Laiin, die ein Dikasterium des Heiligen Stuhls leiten wird.

spiegel.title: Ghosting bei der Jobsuche: Danke für Ihre Bewerbung. Wir melden uns nie.
spiegel.description: Eine Absage ist schnell geschrieben. Trotzdem melden sich viele Unternehmen nie wieder auf eine Bewerbung. Für Arbeitssuchende fühlt sich das mies an – und Arbeitgeber schaden sich damit letztlich selbst.

spiegel.title: Ebola: Behörden sagen WM-Test der DR Kongo gegen Chile in Spanien ab
spiegel.description: Kurz vor der Fußball-Weltmeisterschaft fällt das Vorbereitungsspiel der Kongolesen in La Línea aus. Die Behörden verweisen auf gesundheitliche Vorsichtsmaßnahmen.

spiegel.title: Miete frisst bei 3,2 Millionen Haushalten mehr als 40 Prozent des Einkommens
spiegel.description: Millionen Mieter in Deutschland sind laut einer Studie von ihren Wohnkosten überlastet. Der Mieterbund spricht von alarmierenden Zahlen. Das Statistische Bundesamt schätzt die Lage etwas besser ein.

spiegel.title: Ötzi: Ist die berühmte Gletschermumie in Gefahr?
spiegel.description: Manche sind uralt, andere stammen aus jüngerer Zeit: Auf dem Eismann Ötzi siedeln zahlreiche Bakterien und Pilze. Einige könnten aktiv sein und die Mumie womöglich schleichend zersetzen.

spiegel.title: Rentenreform: Abschaffung der »Rente mit 63« könnte laut Studie fast zehn Milliarden Euro sparen
spiegel.description: 9,5 Milliarden Euro an Einsparungen, 125.000 erhaltene Arbeitskräfte: Das Forschungsinstitut DIW nennt gewichtige Argumente für ein Aus der »Rente mit 63«. Allerdings seien Sonderregeln nötig.

spiegel.title: Brandenburg: Etwa 3000 Menschen müssen ihre Häuser wegen einer Bombensprengungen verlassen
spiegel.description: In Brandenburg sollen zwei Weltkriegsbomben und eine Panzerabwehrmine kontrolliert gesprengt werden. Tausende Anwohner müssen sich vorsorglich in Sicherheit bringen.

spiegel.title: Jill Biden bedauert, nicht über die Drogensucht ihres Sohnes gesprochen zu haben
spiegel.description: Die Drogensucht ihres Sohnes Hunter war für die ehemalige First Lady der USA ein schwerer Schlag. »Ich glaube, wir haben es teilweise verdrängt«, sagt Jill Biden heute. Seit ihr Mann an Krebs erkrankte, sieht sie vieles anders.

spiegel.title: SpaceX: Elon Musks Raketenfirma will offenbar Börsengang für 135 Dollar je Aktie
spiegel.description: Die Raketenfirma SpaceX plant laut einem Agenturbericht einen hohen Ausgabepreis beim anstehenden Börsengang. Für viele Investoren ist es eine Wette auf Firmenchef Elon Musk und dessen ambivalente Erfolgsbilanz.

spiegel.title: Zölle: Donald Trump müsste 85 Milliarden Dollar zurückzahlen – doch er sträubt sich
spiegel.description: Statt eine simple Onlineerstattung für die Rückzahlung rechtswidriger Zölle zu ermöglichen, will US-Präsident Trump einzelne Firmen zum Klagen zwingen. Was das für Konzerne wie DHL, Ford und Walmart und deren Kunden bedeutet.

spiegel.title: Elektroauto gebraucht kaufen: Angebot sinkt, Nachfrage steigt – wann man trotzdem zuschlagen sollte
spiegel.description: Elektroautos aus zweiter Hand sind so gefragt wie nie. Viele Modelle sind deshalb schnell verkauft, das Angebot schrumpft bereits spürbar. Wie finden Interessierte trotzdem ihr Lieblingsmodell?

spiegel.title: Paul McCartney und Mick Jagger sind jetzt Greise: Von welchem kann man lernen, cool zu altern?
Uno-Sicherheitsrat: Wenn Deutschland heute scheitert, ist es auch Wadephuls Verantwortung
spiegel.description: Tauschgeschäfte und Überzeugungsarbeit: Außenminister Johann Wadephul kämpft bis zuletzt um einen deutschen Platz im Uno-Sicherheitsrat. An diesem Mittwoch zeigt sich, ob er Erfolg hat. Das ist alles andere als sicher.

spiegel.title: News: Zitterpartie um Sitz im Sicherheitsrat, Gerhard Schröder in Moskau, nächster Akt in Trumps Zoll-Drama
spiegel.description: Deutschland will wieder in die mächtigste Runde der Weltgemeinschaft. Gerhard Schröder wird in Moskau gesichtet. Und: der nächste Akt in Trumps Zolldrama. Das ist die Lage am Mittwochmorgen.

spiegel.title: ETF: In wenigen Schritten zum ersten eigenen Indexfonds
spiegel.description: Indexfonds gelten als einfachste Möglichkeit, langfristig Vermögen aufzubauen – doch der Anfang fällt manchmal schwer. Diese Schritt-für-Schritt-Anleitung führt Sie zum Ziel.

spiegel.title: Kinderdepots: So sparen Eltern mit Aktienvermögen für ihre Kinder Steuern
spiegel.description: Sebastian L. hat über die Jahre mit Aktieninvestments ein üppiges Vermögen für seine Kinder aufgebaut. Hier erzählt er, warum er ETFs meidet und wie sich mit Kinderdepots ordentlich Steuern sparen lassen.

letemps.description:
A Hambourg, un homme aurait fait subir des sévices à sa femme durant 16 ans. Claudia Wuttke dit n’avoir aucun souvenir des faits, qui ont été filmés. Le délai de prescription est de 5 ans en Allemagne pour des viols commis sans circonstances aggravantes

letemps.description: HEIDI.NEWS. La justice a peut-être confondu deux soirées, se trompant de coupables. Mais elle n'a pas été aidée: les souvenirs de la victime et des suspects sont flous, contradictoires, sans doute altérés par la drogue et la fête

letemps.title: La voiture autonome face à la complexité du réel
letemps.description:
Le Forum de l’ACA a réuni hier près de 400 personnes du monde de l’assurance au SwissTech Convention Center de l’EPFL pour porter un regard sur le futur, et notamment sur la mobilité du futur. L’arrivée des voitures autonomes pourrait bouleverser le modèle actuel de l’assurance automobile

letemps.title: Attirée par la faiblesse du titre, une société d’investissement américaine convoite EasyJet
letemps.description:
Lundi, le titre de la compagnie à bas coûts britannique remontait brusquement après une annonce d’un potentiel rachat par Castlelake. Sous pression face à l’envolée des coûts du kérosène, la société a vu sa perte nette s’aggraver de 27% au premier semestre

letemps.title: Suisse à 10 millions: «La ville est diabolisée, alors que ce sont les maisons individuelles qui font le plus de mal à l’environnement»
letemps.description:
CHRONIQUE. L’initiative de l’UDC fustige les centres urbains qui, sous la pression de la migration, détruiraient le paysage. En réalité, ce sont les habitations en pleine campagne qui nuisent le plus aux verts pâturages. Notre chroniqueuse interroge cette méprise longtemps entretenue par les associations de protection de la nature

letemps.title: Après un revers devant la Cour suprême, Donald Trump relance sa guerre commerciale et vise la Suisse

phys-org.title: Wading bird populations in the New York–New Jersey Harbor are in decline
phys-org.description: Urban estuaries can support thriving ecosystems despite bustling human activity. Noting that bird populations can serve as a key indicator of environmental health, researchers recently investigated trends in the New York–New Jersey Harbor, home to the largest breeding population of colonial nesting wading birds (herons, egrets, ibises) in the northeastern United States.

phys-org.title: Are JWST's early, overmassive black holes just normal-range outliers?
phys-org.description: Ever since the JWST revealed a population of SMBH in the early universe that were overmassive, scientists have been working hard to explain them. These black holes existed when the universe was only about 2 billion years old, during Cosmic Noon, and according to our models of black hole growth, there simply wasn't enough time for them to grow so massive.

phys-org.title: Locked-in food system slows Europe's green shift, article warns
phys-org.description: Europe's agrifood system is under severe pressure. Climate change is causing droughts and floods, and agriculture is putting pressure on nature, the climate and the environment. Diet-related lifestyle diseases are placing a growing burden on health care systems. At the same time, agriculture is expected to deliver affordable food, climate action, biodiversity and food security all at once while maintaining competitiveness in a global market.

phys-org.title: How heavy can a neutron star get?
phys-org.description: The physics of neutron stars are almost too fantastic to believe: something the weight of two suns compacted to a sphere the size of a city. Each teaspoon of its material would weigh billions of tons. If you've done any reading on the topic, you've heard these facts before. But despite the intense interest these extreme objects hold, we are still actively learning lots about them.

phys-org.title: Wetlands loss has increased residential flood insurance claim payments by $10 billion across the US, study finds
phys-org.description: A new study published in Nature Water finds that wetland loss across the United States has increased residential flood insurance claim payments by more than $10 billion since 1985, underscoring the critical role wetlands play in reducing riverine flood damage.

phys-org.title: Terahertz imaging maps spatial chirality in materials with 100-micrometer resolution
phys-org.description: In nature, there exist structures that are mirror images of each other but cannot be perfectly superimposed. These are known as chiral objects, derived from the Greek word for "hand," since left and right hands share the same relationship. Although similar in structure, chiral molecules exhibit different behaviors, and chirality is central to life itself. phys-org.title: Violent rocket particles could reshape future spacecraft design
phys-org.description: When rockets fire into space, the insides of their engines become an extreme environment where temperatures soar and tiny particles are thrown around at hypersonic speeds. These particles behave in ways that break long-held assumptions, according to new research that could help improve the durability, safety and performance of future space and defense technologies.

phys-org.title: Girl power: Red-shouldered hawk parents invest more in female offspring
phys-org.description: A new study published in the Journal of Raptor Research, titled "Factors Influencing Nestling Sex Ratios of Suburban and Rural Red-Shouldered Hawks, 2004–2016," finds that hawk parents prioritize producing female offspring when conditions are optimal. This means that higher quality territories could result in more females, offering biologists clues about habitat health, which is important intel as the species adapts to urban environments with increasing frequency.

phys-org.title: Leafy camouflage reshapes katydid love songs, making males more attractive to females
phys-org.description: New research from the University of St Andrews has discovered that insects who conceal themselves as leaves also use their leafy camouflage to amplify mating calls, making themselves more attractive to the opposite sex. The research published in Proceedings of the Royal Society B is the first demonstration of how impressive leaf mimicry can also be used to enhance the attractiveness of a sexual signal.

phys-org.title: Ötzi the Iceman and his microbiome—a 5,300-year-old relationship
phys-org.description: Researchers at Eurac Research have obtained a detailed picture of the microbial community associated with Ötzi, Europe's oldest known natural human mummy. The study provides insights into a complex microbiome, ranging from the gut flora of a Copper Age human to cold-adapted yeasts.

phys-org.title: Sharks thrive in hotspots of prey, underlining need for holistic approach to conservation
phys-org.description: Sharks need healthy habitats, and some have a strong preference for locations jam-packed with food, according to FIU research. A recent study of Caribbean reef sharks in the Bahamas, where shark fishing has been banned for years, shows that the sharks don't seem to like places where prey is hard to find. Instead, they prefer to live where prey is most abundant. The research is published in the journal Animal Conservation.

phys-org.title: Biomaterial made from jackfruit latex is a promising treatment for periodontitis
phys-org.description: Researchers from the Faculty of Medical and Health Sciences (FCMS) at the Pontifical Catholic University of São Paulo (PUC-SP) in Sorocaba, in the interior of the state of São Paulo, Brazil, have developed a biomaterial containing jackfruit latex, pomegranate peel extract, and simvastatin (a statin-based medication) that shows promising efficacy in treating periodontitis.

phys-org.title: Strain creates moiré 2D materials without twisting or stacking, opening more scalable route
phys-org.description: Cornell researchers have developed a new way to create moiré patterns—atomic-scale structures that can give materials unusual quantum behaviors—without relying on the traditionally used difficult-to-control twisting and stacking methods. The study is published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

phys-org.title: Climate-based tool predicts coral bleaching months in advance, offering critical lead time for reef protection
phys-org.description: Researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) have developed a new method to predict coral bleaching five to six months before it occurs, giving reef managers valuable time to protect vulnerable ecosystems. phys-org.title: Organic farming surges in Andalusia, driven by both conviction and commercial appeal
phys-org.description: Among the goals it has set for 2030, the European Union aims to ensure that at least one quarter of agricultural land is farmed using organic or ecological practices. In this race, Andalusia holds a significant advantage: over 50% of Spain's organic farming is concentrated in the south, making its lands a testing ground for policies that encourage and promote these practices. Until now, however, the motivations behind choosing organic practices over others had not been thoroughly studied. A

phys-org.title: Atomic reshuffle leads to record-breaking catalysts for hydrogen production
phys-org.description: Researchers have discovered that atoms can be mixed, separated, and recombined within the same experiment, providing a pathway to a record-breaking catalyst for green hydrogen production. In their study, the team created nanoscale particles containing only a few dozen platinum and nickel atoms and observed unusual dynamic behavior in direct space and in real time. As the two metals separate from one another while maintaining an interface, they become highly active for electrochemical water split

phys-org.title: City birds dazzle females with 'borrowed' human items
phys-org.description: Bowerbirds in an Australian city use a range of human items—from glass and plastic to banknotes and even a pair of handcuffs—to impress females, shows new research in Royal Society Open Science. Male bowerbirds create an intricate tunnel of twigs called a bower, then gather colorful items to show to any females that visit.

phys-org.title: Forest resident birds avoid intensive clearcuts, acoustic monitoring shows
phys-org.description: New research reveals that resident forest birds avoid intensive clearcut areas, highlighting the need for more sustainable forestry practices.

new-sci.title: Ötzi's frozen remains may harbour metabolically active microbes
new-sci.description: Researchers studying a 5300-year-old mummified man have identified bacteria that lived in his gut when he was alive, as well as cold-tolerant fungi that colonised his body after death

new-sci.title: Why you need to future proof your brain in middle age and how to start
new-sci.description: Ages 40 to 65 see a period of turmoil in the brain that has previously been overlooked. But identifying problems during this time can protect your cognitive health for decades to come

new-sci.title: How the electromagnetic spectrum opened our eyes to the universe
new-sci.description: Our understanding of the electromagnetic spectrum goes back to Isaac Newton, but astronomers are still finding new ways to employ it. Astrophysicist Emma Chapman explores how much these invisible waves can reveal to us about the cosmos – and whether they might show us that we’re not alone

new-sci.title: The best new popular science books of June 2026
new-sci.description: The most exciting popular science reads this month explore everything from symbiosis to hormones, while Alice Roberts takes on an editor-in-chief role in her latest book

new-sci.title: Hearing loss is bad for the whole body – but new treatments are coming
new-sci.description: From dementia to heart attacks, hearing loss has been linked to a wide range of effects across the body, and the condition is on the rise. Fortunately, we're learning how best to safeguard this crucial sense and how we might be able to reverse the damage

new-sci.title: Hidden store of manganese may have helped Earth get its oxygen
new-sci.description: Computer simulations have uncovered a new manganese compound that could exist deep in Earth’s mantle and may be connected to the process that gave our atmosphere oxygen

new-sci.title: New Scientist recommends Togetherness, a radical new view of life
new-sci.description: An exploration of how biological cooperation underpins all life - and why we’ve overlooked its power until now - makes thrilling reading, finds Penny Sarchet

new-sci.title: A golden age of maths is dawning and mathematicians are freaking out
new-sci.description: Mathematicians are stunned at the progress AI is making in solving advanced problems, leaving some questioning whether there will still be room for humans

new-sci.title: 'Transformative' pancreatic cancer drug doubles survival time
new-sci.description: People with advanced pancreatic cancer taking an experimental daily pill lived nearly twice as long as those receiving chemotherapy infusions

new-sci.title: How human error became a weapon against large language models
new-sci.description: Alan Turing proposed a test for machine intelligence: could a computer convince a human it was human? We have begun conducting the same test on ourselves, writes Max Moser

new-sci.title: Do turmeric and curcumin have any actual health benefits?
new-sci.description: Turmeric is heralded for its anti-cancer and anti-inflammatory properties, but columnist Alice Klein finds that the evidence for this is shaky. Taking high doses of its curcumin extract in supplement form can be risky

new-sci.title: Huge study of Alzheimer’s genetics identifies new drug targets
new-sci.description: Almost 50 more genes have been flagged as being linked to Alzheimer’s, along with changes in activity in crucial cells that disappear as dementia progresses

new-sci.title: Capitalism has warped our understanding of ecology and life’s origins
new-sci.description: The ideas of survival of the fittest and winning at all costs are closely entwinned with Darwinism, but they shouldn’t be. A rethink from a more communal perspective is in order

new-sci.title: Geoengineering can thicken Arctic sea ice, but for how long?
new-sci.description: Two companies are aiming to preserve Arctic ice by pumping water onto the sheet and letting it freeze, but only one of the trials found that this delayed melting in the summer

new-sci.title: Pancreatic cancer halted by virus injection in three patients
new-sci.description: A cancer-killing virus has stopped pancreatic tumours from growing and spreading in three people in an initial safety trial, raising hopes that it may help to beat the deadly condition

new-sci.title: How a radical new view of life could reveal its origin – and aliens
new-sci.description: We've been looking at nature the wrong way, argues Rowan Hooper. If we stop focusing on the individual, we get a whole new picture of how life on Earth – and elsewhere – may have begun

new-sci.title: Embryos made without sperm or eggs reveal why many pregnancies fail
new-sci.description: Embryo organoids made from stem cells are enabling scientists to recreate early pregnancy in the lab, unlocking treatments for infertility, miscarriage and pre-eclampsia

new-sci.title: The best new science-fiction books of June 2026
new-sci.description: There is plenty of intriguing sci-fi on offer this month, whether it’s solar-powered cities from Adrian Tchaikovsky or a strange future from M. John Harrison

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

undark.title: Medicine’s Move Toward Race-Neutral Risk Assessments
undark.description: Earlier this year, new guidelines were released for doctors assessing a patient’s risk for heart disease. The guidelines take a race-neutral and patient-informed approach that’s rooted in up-to-date science, one doctor writes, and offer a glimpse of a future in which health equity is the standard in medicine.

undark.title: In Coal Country, Black Lung Surges as Federal Protections Stall
undark.description: While the Trump administration is directing hundreds of millions of dollars to coal projects, miners in Appalachia are suffering from a resurgence of black lung disease. But industry pushback is delaying federal rules that would reduce miners’ exposure to deadly silica dust.

public-dom.title: Animal, Vegetable, Lamb: The Zoophyte from Tartary
public-dom.description: In the Middle Ages, rumours spread across Europe of a strange hybrid creature, half-animal, half-plant, known as the Vegetable Lamb of Tartary. A hoax based on fern rhizomes? A euphemism for culled fetal lambs? Or perhaps a medieval misapprehension of cotton? Thom Sliwowski traces the roots of this fabled zoophyte.

public-dom.title: The Prophecies of the Brahan Seer (1877)
public-dom.description: Historical predictions from the Scottish Nostradamus.

public-dom.title: “Plaything of the Gods”: Photographs of Pushball (early 1900s)
public-dom.description: Photographs and films of a forgotten pastime.

public-dom.title: Twilight of the Velocipede: Typesetting Races before the Age of Linotype
public-dom.description: Before Linotype revolutionised typesetting in the 1880s, compositors set texts by hand — and they set them *fast*. Alex Wright rediscovers the thrilling world of typesetting races, which drew crowds in the thousands, offered huge cash prizes, and helped women "Swifts" fight for workplace equity.

public-dom.title: Pyramid of the Capitalist System (1911)
public-dom.description: The working class undergirds everything in this cartoon of capitalist society.

public-dom.title: Magic by Return of Post: How Mail Order Delivered the Occult
public-dom.description: What allowed occultism to blossom in the United States at the turn of the 20th century? Linotype machines, cheap pulp paper, and newly improved postal networks. Allan Johnson investigates the forgotten history and (still living) world of mail-order magic.

proj-syn.title: British Steel Needs a Transformation, Not a Bailout
proj-syn.description: The recent revival of industrial policy offers an opportunity to break the old pattern whereby economic risks are socialized while rewards remain privatized. In addition to attaching meaningful conditionalities to public support, governments must invest in the state capacity required to govern strategic sectors well.

proj-syn.title: How to Encourage Deceased Organ Donation
proj-syn.description: Developing countries facing organ shortages often search for complex solutions, such as sweeping legal reforms. But Tunisia’s experience suggests a much simpler first step: awareness-raising sessions where doctors explain how the transplant system works, and people share their fears and concerns.

proj-syn.title: Building Alliances of America’s Allies
proj-syn.description: In a world in which the US cannot be counted on as it once was, the objective is not stability at any price, but rather stability on terms consistent with national and Western interests. This is achievable, but only if the friends of the US recognize the new reality and act individually and collectively to meet the challenge.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Limits of African Data Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: African countries are recognizing that no matter how well-designed their data-protection regulations are, their sovereignty over US-based Big Tech firms ends at the boundary between subsidiary and parent. Overcoming this barrier will require a level of coordination that the continent has yet to achieve.

proj-syn.title: The AI Economy’s Permanent Underclass
proj-syn.description: AI is transforming the global economy while widening the gap between technological winners and losers. Governments that fail to secure a place in the AI supply chain may find themselves confronting mass job displacement without the tax revenues or state capacity needed to contain the social and political fallout.

proj-syn.title: The Rape of Venezuela
proj-syn.description: Venezuela’s oil production is rising, yet its currency is depreciating, inflation is accelerating, and foreign exchange remains scarce. The disconnect reflects a political economy built on private dealmaking and a mutually beneficial alliance between ruling elites and US President Donald Trump’s acolytes.

proj-syn.title: The One Man Who Could Give Trump Middle East Peace
proj-syn.description: With a large majority of UN member states recognizing Palestine on the 1967 lines, there is a clear international blueprint for creating an independent Palestinian state alongside Israel. What has been missing is credible Palestinian leadership of the kind that the imprisoned politician Marwan Barghouti could provide.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Nuclear Options
proj-syn.description: The risks raised by nuclear weapons remain as potent as ever, but the institutional framework that mitigated them has been severely eroded. The task now is to prevent deterrence from giving way to proliferation—which, for Europe, means building conventional capabilities, keeping the US engaged, and upholding restraint.

proj-syn.title: The Intelligence That AI Is Missing
proj-syn.description: For AI to simplify humans’ complex social and professional lives, it cannot just give tidy answers based on whatever the internet has to say about our values. It will need the capacity to account for our relational commitments, which are typically grounded in personal identity, experience, and culture.

proj-syn.title: Why Isn’t Europe Poorer Than the US?
proj-syn.description: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman has a point when he says that European living standards have largely kept pace with those in the US, despite flagging growth and innovation. But this will not remain true indefinitely: restoring Europe's ability to compete at the technological frontier remains essential to its future well-being.

proj-syn.title: The Real Choice Confronting Developing Countries
proj-syn.description: Lost in the debate about whether developing countries should pursue manufacturing- or services-led growth is the potential for new AI tools to make even informal workers far more productive. If governments can broaden access to such technologies, they no longer need to choose between strategies.

proj-syn.title: India’s Great Political Realignment
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party’s focus on religious identity, together with its “purification” of voter rolls, has created a more binary—and potentially volatile—political landscape, where elections increasingly reflect ethno-religious identity. This month’s elections in five states largely confirmed this trend.

proj-syn.title: Central Banking in an Age of Global Supply Shocks
proj-syn.description: The core assumptions underlying the decades-old inflation-targeting orthodoxy have proven to be unfit for a geopolitically fragmented world characterized by frequent supply-side disruptions. Under such conditions, central banks' traditional monetary policies are only as effective as markets believe them to be.

proj-syn.title: The Tech-MAGA Breakup Is Coming
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump has managed to fuse a backward-looking populist movement with a Silicon Valley vanguard whose guiding assumption is that AI will render a large share of ordinary people economically redundant.
